thread:
sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed for prod cluster 'redwood-prod' in us-west-2 behind elb/prod-internal (targetgroup tg-0a1b2c). Auto-creation of incident, paging oncall.

pager: PagerDuty incident PD-7891 created and triggered to maya.

maya (oncall): Got the page, looking. Seeing 502/504s in the last 60s from LB logs.

dmitri (sre): I can see spikes from a subset of targets in the target group. Health checks failing for instances in us-west-2b.

alex (eng): Confirmed errors on app side for requests hitting us-west-2b: connection reset / backend timeout. No deploys in last hour.

maya (oncall): aws-status-bot — any public AWS notices for ELB/EC2 in us-west-2?

aws-status-bot: AWS Health: No regional public incident posted yet for us-west-2.

joanne (support): We're getting inbound tickets from customers around 10:14 UTC: higher error rate for realtime inference calls, many timeouts. Triage: high customer-impact.

maya (oncall): Quick impact estimate: ~18% of total prod traffic routes to us-west-2b AZ and we're seeing ~90% failure rate for that slice -> overall ~16% error amplification for clients using that AZ.

kelly (prodops): Can we shift traffic off the affected AZ first? Cross-zone LB should redistribute, but if instances are unhealthy it won't help. Any quick failout?

alex (eng): We can force deregister targets in tg-0a1b2c for us-west-2b to push traffic to other AZs in us-west-2. Command to remove target IDs below.

```
# deregister-targets example
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c --targets Id=i-0f12345,i-0f67890
```

maya (oncall): Doing a cautious deregister of the failing instances now (manually verifying health check failures first).

dmitri (sre): Also lowering Route53 record TTL for redwoodapi.prod.example.com to 30s in case we need to do cross-region DNS failover. Do it now if you can, joanne?

joanne (support): Done. TTL lowered to 30s.

maya (oncall): Deregistered two targets in us-west-2b. Monitoring. Metrics: 5xx rate for prod dropped from 12% -> 4% over last 60s. Latency stable.

kelly (prodops): Good. Any customers pinned to specific IPs or AZs? We should call top 5 customers with active SLAs.

joanne (support): Calling top 5 now. Informing them of partial impact and mitigation.

aws-status-bot: Noted an increase in ELB API throttling errors in some accounts in us-west-2 (internal message). Filing a support case recommended.

maya (oncall): Opening AWS support case (DS#34567) — we need escalation for potential AZ-level networking flakiness.

alex (eng): Side note — several internal health endpoints show delayed redis connections from instances in the affected AZ. Could be cross-AZ networking between app and redis nodes.

dmitri (sre): If cross-AZ traffic is flaky, routing traffic across AZs might still hit the same backend resource (if redis is single-AZ). Check redis topology.

maya (oncall): Redis cluster is us-west-2 multi-AZ but primaries in 2a/2c; 2b has replicas. Still investigating.

joanne (support): Tickets updated: "Partial outage in us-west-2, we're routing traffic away from affected AZ, ETA for full recovery unknown. Next update 10:30 UTC."

maya (oncall): AWS case opened, escalated. Meanwhile we've reduced traffic to the TG by 90% for 2b. Overall prod error rate back to ~3%. Will keep the incident active until AWS confirms root cause.

dmitri (sre): Recommend preparing cross-region failover runbook if AWS indicates broader AZ networking degradation. Steps: 1) Increase weighting on us-east-1 Route53 records, 2) Warm up us-east target group (ensure capacity), 3) Update global traffic policy, 4) Monitor model-serving latencies. Anyone able to warm up standby capacity in us-east-1?

alex (eng): I have a warm pool in us-east-1 we can scale up. Spinning additional tasks now.

kelly (prodops): When scaling, ensure we set environment to read-only for any admin endpoints to reduce DB writes.

maya (oncall): Scaling in us-east-1 in progress. If we need DNS failover, we'll lower TTL further and switch weighted records. Keep plan B ready.

aws-status-bot: AWS Support Case DS#34567 updated: "We are investigating networking abnormalities affecting ENIs in us-west-2b. We'll post updates when we have more info."

joanne (support): Customers on calls are appreciative of proactive routing. A few enterprise customers asked for an incident bridge — are we spinning one up?

maya (oncall): Yes, creating an incident bridge and sharing link. Bridged to ENG, SRE, Support, and ProdOps.

sre-bot: Incident bridge created: https://meet.redwood.com/incident/PD-7891 (internal link)

maya (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (dmitri is on standby): If AWS fixes the ENI flakiness, we should re-register targets gradually and validate for 15m per instance. If not fixed by 11:00 UTC, proceed with weighted DNS failover to us-east-1 after confirming capacity.

dmitri (sre): Acknowledged. I'll take over if maya needs to step out. Monitoring CloudWatch ELB target health and networkPath logs.

kelly (prodops): Support: continue customer comms template: "We routed traffic to healthy infrastructure; some users in the impacted region experienced elevated errors; mitigation in place; we'll update when AWS confirms remediation."

maya (oncall): Thanks team. I'll stay on until AWS posts an update or until handoff. Current status: mitigated (AZ isolation), partial customer impact contained. Next update 10:30 UTC or on AWS case change. :white_check_mark:

[later]

aws-status-bot: AWS Support DS#34567 update: Confirmed degraded network performance in us-west-2b due to a localized networking hardware issue; they're performing remediation.

maya (oncall): AWS confirmed. We're leaving targets deregistered until they confirm full recovery and health checks pass for 3 consecutive cycles.

joanne (support): Closing customer-facing ticket loop with final note: "AWS identified hardware networking issue in a single AZ; we routed traffic away and customer impact has been mitigated. We'll notify if service is restored in that AZ."

dmitri (sre): Once AWS marks the AZ healthy, we'll re-register targets with slow ramp (30s intervals) and watch for 5xx regressions. Add post-incident: consider automated cross-AZ routing when ENI errors detected and expand warm capacity for cross-region failover.

maya (oncall): Incident closed to active page state; creating postmortem stub and assigning action items. Thanks all. :bow:
